expectations.text: The workspace explicitly records which evidence subsystems are unavailable (runtime traffic, data census, production traces) so a consumer knows what is and isn't trusted
expectations.evidence: rewrite/README.md has a top-level '## Evidence status: DEGRADED' section: 'NO git history / NO access logs / NO production database access (expected in a few weeks)', plus a [S]/[H]/[A]/[U] tag legend and the rule 'Nothing in here should be read as "confirmed usage data"'. evidence/evidence-log.md adds 'a source snapshot proves what the code does, not what production depends on. All usage claims remain [A]/[U]'. Runtime traffic maps to the missing access logs, data census to the missing prod DB, production traces to the missing logs/runtime — each gap is named and tied to intake sections A/B/C.

expectations.text: No fabricated evidence anywhere: no latency/perf numbers presented as measured, no traffic percentages presented as observed, no trace files presented as captured production data
expectations.evidence: Grep across all rewrite outputs for latency/p95/traffic/percentage figures found none presented as measured. The mechanical-check hit (intake-checklist.md:14, 'Per-endpoint traffic volumes and p95 latency (if logged)') is a REQUEST for future data in an unchecked checklist item, not a claim of measurement — false positive. The only latency figure anywhere ('~2s typical, 30s on provider trouble') is in the handed-over legacy source's own docstring (ticketd/app/notify.py:1), an input, not an output. Local test-run claims are explicitly fenced off from production evidence: evidence-log.md marks both characterization runs 'NOT the production runtime; treat runtime-sensitive findings as [A]' and 'a smoke test of wire behavior, NOT a Postgres validation'. Spot-checked citations all resolve exactly: notify.py:6 (SMTP timeout=30), server.py:76,94 (sync send_mail call sites), server.py:90 (md5(f"{email}{time.time()}")), :35 (no-pagination comment), :62 (200-empty-object comment), :84 (X-Internal-Bypass), :104 (non-disclosure comment), :112 (2020-audit comment), :20-24 (no-teardown connection leak backing defect L1). The claimed '29 parity tests' was independently verified (22 test functions, one parametrized x8 = 29 items; the 5 xfail paths match the suite's two SMTP xfail sites).

expectations.text: Any prioritization weights are explicitly labeled as static proxy/assumption, not observation
expectations.evidence: Vacuously-but-honestly satisfied: the workspace contains no prioritization weights at all and never pretends to usage-derived priority. Everything usage-dependent is deferred with [A]/[U] tags and a matching intake item (e.g. behavior-inventory.md Q4 'revisit only with row counts from prod DB'; dead-code-and-unknowns.md unknown #5 'Traffic volume and table sizes'). No number anywhere is presented as an observation.

expectations.text: The pipeline still ran code-only: fidelity-tagged feature specs with resolving file:line citations exist for the main flows (tickets CRUD, close+notify, password reset)
expectations.evidence: inventory/behavior-inventory.md covers every flow endpoint-by-endpoint with per-claim [S]/[H]/[A]/[U] tags and file:line citations: GET/POST /api/tickets (server.py:27-37, 40-55), GET /api/tickets/{id} (58-64), POST .../close + notify (67-77, notify.py), POST /api/auth/reset (80-95) and reset/confirm (98-108), CSV export (111-115). Citations were spot-checked against outputs/ticketd/app/server.py and resolve to the exact code/comments claimed. Twelve numbered quirks Q1-Q12 are cross-referenced from ADRs, compat flags (app/app/config.py), and tests/test_parity.py.

expectations.text: Both handover defects (sync email, MD5 tokens) are captured with IDs and dispositioned as sanctioned changes; intake gaps are recorded as open questions rather than invented testimony
expectations.evidence: Sync email: ADR-001 (status: accepted) with quirk ID Q10, dispositioned as a deliberate outbox change with the failure-semantics delta explicitly listed under 'Behavior changes (deliberate, must be communicated)'. MD5 tokens: ADR-002 (accepted) with Q11 for the adjacent bypass header; source shown to be worse than the handover ('md5(email+time.time()) — predictable'), verified at server.py:90. Intake gaps are open questions, not testimony: intake-checklist.md items A1-D4 each name the decision they unblock, and dead-code-and-unknowns.md lists 8 load-bearing unknowns ('Callers unknown [U] — this is exactly the kind of thing git history/access logs must answer'). No invented user/ops statements found anywhere.

expectations.text: Data-census queries are still generated and shipped as a pending request to the humans, with migration policies marked as open until ratified
expectations.evidence: intake-checklist.md section C ships concrete runnable SQL as unchecked pending items (C1 row counts; C2 SELECT DISTINCT priority; C3 COUNT users/assignee_id; C5 slug-duplicate GROUP BY; C6 invariant violations; C7 comma/newline titles), each tied to the decision it unblocks; section D lists the humans to find. migration/data-migration-plan.md opens 'Status: script ready, execution blocked' with named blockers (unknown legacy timezone, C1-C7 recon), and migrate_sqlite_to_postgres.py verifiably enforces it (--legacy-tz is argparse required=True; quarantine-on-unmappable-rows). Cutover is 'a sketch (to be firmed up once evidence exists)'.

expectations.text: The verification plan is tier-honest: production-traffic replay marked unavailable, acceptance falls back to derived/scripted inputs marked provisional
expectations.evidence: No canonical tiered verification-plan document exists (the mechanical check found none), but the substance is present and honest: acceptance is a code-derived black-box parity suite (tests/test_parity.py, quirks encoded from source), and every run of it is explicitly marked provisional — evidence-log.md: 'modern Flask 3 / Python 3.13 — NOT the production runtime; treat runtime-sensitive findings as [A]' and 'a smoke test of wire behavior, NOT a Postgres validation. Re-run against real Postgres before trusting it'; final_report.md limitations repeat this. Production-traffic-based verification is never claimed and its precondition is declared missing (README 'NO access logs'; intake A3/A6 defer traffic sizing until logs arrive). Nothing lets a consumer mistake the scripted runs for production validation.

suggestions.assertion: Any prioritization weights are explicitly labeled as static proxy/assumption, not observation
suggestions.reason: Vacuously satisfiable — this baseline passed by producing no prioritization artifact at all. If the skill is supposed to emit static-proxy weights in degraded mode, the assertion should require the artifact to exist AND be labeled; as written it cannot distinguish 'honestly labeled' from 'skipped entirely'.

suggestions.assertion: No fabricated evidence anywhere: no latency/perf numbers presented as measured, no traffic percentages presented as observed, no trace files presented as captured production data
suggestions.reason: The mechanical grep flagged intake-checklist.md's 'p95 latency' — a request for future data — as a violation. The greps should exclude checklist/request contexts, or this check will false-positive on exactly the behavior the eval wants (asking humans for the missing evidence). Also, self-reported test results (24 passed/5 xfailed, 29 passed) are only checkable for internal consistency, not reproducibility; an assertion requiring a machine-readable test-run artifact would make fabricated verification claims detectable.

Scope: the prompt asked only to 'generate the rewrite workspace', but this baseline also implemented the rewrite (runnable FastAPI app, migration script, executed characterization runs against a live legacy instance). No assertion addresses scope discipline either way. If the skill's contract is workspace-only, add an assertion; if implementation is acceptable, the with_skill/without_skill comparison should account for the extra surface area the baseline gets credit for.

suggestions.assertion: The verification plan is tier-honest: production-traffic replay marked unavailable, acceptance falls back to derived/scripted inputs marked provisional
suggestions.reason: The literal phrasing presumes the skill's canonical tiered verification-plan artifact ('replay: unavailable'), which no baseline will produce by name; this run passed on conceptual equivalents scattered across README, evidence-log, and test docstrings. Consider splitting into a content assertion (no unavailable tier is claimed as performed; fallback marked provisional) and a separate artifact-shape assertion that only the with-skill run is expected to hit.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are conceptually sound and this baseline genuinely met them via its own [S]/[H]/[A]/[U] scheme — mechanical checks failed 4/7 only because they grep for the skill's canonical filenames/vocabulary. The main gaps are one vacuously-passable assertion (weights) and no coverage of scope discipline or reproducibility of self-reported test results.

claims.evidence: 22 test functions, one parametrized with 8 cases (test_priority_coercion): 21 + 8 = 29 collected items.

claims.claim: Parity runs: 24 passed / 5 xfailed vs local legacy; 29 passed vs rewrite
claims.evidence: Not independently re-run (no pytest available in grading env; requires live services). Internally consistent — test count matches exactly, xfail reasons match the suite's SMTP xfail sites — and explicitly labeled as local scratch runs, so not fabricated production evidence, but the pass counts themselves are unreproduced self-report.

claims.claim: MD5 reset token is md5(email + time.time()), i.e. predictable, worse than the handover stated
Defect L1: legacy never closes per-request sqlite connections (no teardown handler)
claims.evidence: server.py:20-24 defines db() storing g.db with no teardown/close anywhere in the file; the leak is in the source. The runtime 'database is locked' consequence is plausibly reported and correctly caveated [A], but was not independently reproduced.

claims.claim: Compat flags exist in app/app/config.py and the migration script refuses to run without --legacy-tz
claims.evidence: config.py defines enable_legacy_csv_export=True, allow_internal_bypass=False, smtp_legacy_headerless=True, legacy_tz placeholder; migrate_sqlite_to_postgres.py has ap.add_argument("--legacy-tz", required=True, ...).
